title: The Day the Welcome Went Missing
paragraphs: On Welcome Day, Mayor Ren discovered a {{1}} {{2}} beside the garden gate, exactly where the town's welcome sign was supposed to be.
Before anyone could explain it, the whole town began to {{3}}.

Hudson was the first to investigate. He searched beneath benches, behind flowerpots, and inside an old {{4}}. He found three lost buttons, a ribbon, and something suspiciously sticky, but absolutely no welcome sign.

Snowy opened her notebook and announced that this was a very {{5}} mystery. She carefully recorded everyone's observations, although she had to remind Hudson twice that guessing was not the same as finding evidence.
Meanwhile, Merry gathered flowers for the celebration. Unfortunately, someone had filled her favorite watering can with {{6}}. She decided not to ask questions.

At Kit's seed shop, customers were arriving with increasingly unusual suggestions. One insisted that the new welcome sign should feature a {{7}}. Another wanted every visitor to {{8}} before entering town.
Phineas examined the empty signposts, measured the wooden frame, and declared that the replacement would have to be especially {{9}}.
Mayor Ren listened to everyone's ideas while attempting to maintain his dignity. Unfortunately, just as he began his official speech, a {{10}} appeared in the middle of the town square.
Nobody could agree whether this was a disaster, a decoration, or an unexpected guest.
By afternoon, the square was filled with petals, paint, ribbons, and laughter. Everyone contributed something, even if some contributions were a little {{11}}.
Finally, the new welcome sign was ready. Mayor Ren climbed onto the platform, lifted his ceremonial ribbon, and invited the entire town to {{12}}.
For a moment, everyone fell silent.
The path was lined with flowers, the windows glowed warmly, and the newly restored sign stood proudly above the garden gate.
The townspeople agreed that nobody would ever forget this Welcome Day.
They weren't entirely sure what had happened.
But they were delighted to have been there.
